result.effect: 1,455 unique axiom identifiers; 1,464 work-axiom mappings; 149 unique works; seven axioms mapped to more than one work, with a maximum of four mappings

cells.quote: "Only seven axioms map to more than one work, with a maximum of four mappings, so the present artifact is better characterized as a set of work-derived records than as a densely reused cross-work ontology."
cells.note: No study text is available; quote copied from the wiki entry. The entry reports a descriptive audit, but does not state a treatment effect, study design, learner characteristics, setting, or duration.

O.outcome_detail: students having to redo the exercise

cells.quote: From these students, 22 had to redo their homework exercise on axiomatic proofs. This is significantly higher than, for example, the number of students in the same group who had to redo the exercise on semantic tableaux: 5 out of 65.
cells.note: Observational comparison of homework exercise types; no random assignment or printed effect size.

O.outcome_detail: describing the energy of a particle after tunnelling

cells.quote: Tutorial students did much better at describing the energy of a particle that has tunnelled through a barrier (see Figure 7).
cells.note: The authors describe the comparison as suggestive rather than conclusive because the groups were small, taught in different semesters, and not randomly assigned.

O.outcome_detail: drawing wave functions without an axis shift

cells.quote: The traditional (lecture-only) students were also much more likely to give the axis shift response in their examination question.
cells.note: The tutorial group was less likely to produce the axis-shift response; the study reports no printed effect size and cautions that the evidence is suggestive, not conclusive.

D.treatment: tunnelling tutorial with small-group guided-inquiry worksheets

O.outcome_detail: description of the energy of particles after tunnelling

cells.quote: Tutorial students did much better at describing the energy of a particle that has tunnelled through a barrier (see Figure 7). Nearly 2/3 of the lecture-only students described energy loss for a particle that has tunnelled through a barrier.
cells.note: The authors describe the evidence as suggestive, not conclusive; groups were small and taught in different semesters.

D.treatment: tunnelling tutorial with small-group guided-inquiry worksheets

O.outcome_detail: appropriate graphical representation of the wave function without an axis shift

cells.quote: The traditional (lecture-only) students were also much more likely to give the axis shift response in their examination question (see Figure 8). As described above, nearly 3/4 (7 of the 11) gave the axis shift response.
cells.note: The authors state that the tutorial students were less likely to assume the axis-shift response, but provide only suggestive evidence.

D.comparison: students not giving the axis-shift response

O.outcome_detail: description of energy loss during tunnelling

cells.quote: All of the students who gave the axis shift response also described energy loss.
cells.note: This was reported for the survey subset of 17 students asked to sketch the wave function; the text does not report the reverse association or a statistical test.
